comments.author: simpaticoder
comments.story_title: Ask HN: What is the best software to visualize a graph with a billion nodes?
comments.quote_zh: 一个相当傻气的 Unix 块设备实现，用的是 ping 延迟
comments.text_zh: Hilbert 曲线（或类似方法）常被用来绘制数十亿个节点的图[1]。不过默认情况下，这不会显示图中节点之间的关系。根据你的数据，也许可以写一个函数，把边列表映射到能暗示邻近关系的节点索引。注意，可视化受人类感知限制，大约只能处理 10000 个元素，更实用的是 1000 个元素。你可以试试力导向图，或许还可以试试分层变体，其中节点可以包含子图。除非你有明显的根节点，否则这种变体会很有意思：用户可以从任意一组节点开始，根据起点不同得到不同的洞察。1 - 摘自 "Harder Drive"，这是一个相当傻气的实现：用 ping 延迟来做 Unix 块设备，连接到任何愿意接受他的主机。他在这个偏移处用 Hilbert 曲线可视化了整个 IPv4 地址空间：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Hilbert curves (or similar) are often used for graphing billions of nodes[1]. However this will not by default show the relationships between nodes in a graph. Depending on your data you may be able to write a function to map from your edge list to a node index that hints at proximity. Note that visualizations are limited by human perception to ~10000 elements, more usefully 1000 elements. You might try a force directed graph, perhaps a hierarchical variant wherein nodes can contain sub-graphs. Unless you have obvious root nodes, this variant would be interesting in that the user could start from an arbitrary set of nodes, giving different insights depending on their starting point. 1 - An excerpt from "Harder Drive", a rather silly implementation of a unix block device using ping latency with any host that will let him. He visualizes the full ipv4 address space in a hilbert curve at this offset: [VIDEO]

comments.author: kmeisthax
comments.story_title: Anubis: Proof-of-work proxy to prevent AI crawlers
comments.quote_zh: 也许 suckerpinch 能把它做进《Harder Drive》的续集里
comments.text_zh: 你可以把 Anubis 变成 Proof of Storage：往 session cookie 里追加大量随机数据，然后在每次请求时对它做哈希。再配合每个 session cookie 的限制，如果 LLM 机器人想抓取你的网站，你实际上就能强迫它们存储你想要的任意数据量。也许 suckerpinch 能把它做进《Harder Drive: Hard drives we didn't want or need》的续集里 [0]。[0] [VIDEO]
comments.text: You can turn Anubis into Proof of Storage by appending large amounts of random data to the session cookie and then hashing it on each request. Combined with per-session-cookie limits, you can effectively force the LLM bots to store all the data you want if they want to scrape your site. Maybe suckerpinch can work it into a sequel to Harder Drive: Hard drives we didn't want or need [0]. [0] [VIDEO]
